sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body:
115. (1) Whoever does any act with the intention of thereby causing hurt to any person, or with the knowledge that he is likely thereby to cause hurt to any person, and does thereby cause hurt to any person, is said “voluntarily to cause hurt”
(2) Whoever, except in the case provided for by sub-section (1) of section 122 voluntarily causes hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both

learningObjectives: Master the substantive offence of voluntarily causing hurt under BNS s. 115.
Analyze the mens rea requirements under sub-section (1): intention or knowledge of causing hurt.
Examine the baseline punishment under sub-section (2): imprisonment up to one year, fine up to ₹10,000, or both.
Understand the compounding and cognizable characteristics of simple hurt.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 115 codifies voluntarily causing hurt: sub-section (1) defines the offence as doing any act with intention of thereby causing hurt to any person, or with knowledge that the doer is likely thereby to cause hurt to any person, and thereby causing hurt; sub-section (2) punishes whoever voluntarily causes hurt with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Enforces criminal sanctions against intentional or knowingly reckless physical assaults that inflict bodily pain, disease, or infirmity upon another person.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 115 (consolidating IPC ss. 321 and 323).
Sub-section (1): Definition — doing an act with intention or knowledge of causing hurt, resulting in hurt.
Sub-section (2): Punishment — imprisonment of either description up to one year, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both (fine increased from ₹1,000 under IPC 323).
Exception: Except in cases provided for by Section 122 (hurt on grave and sudden provocation).
essentialIngredients: The accused caused hurt (bodily pain, disease, or infirmity) to a person.
The accused acted with the intention of causing hurt; OR
The accused acted with the knowledge that he was likely thereby to cause hurt.
The act was voluntary within the meaning of the Sanhita.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 115 consolidates the definition (former IPC 321) and the punishment (former IPC 323) for voluntarily causing simple hurt. The actus reus is the causation of hurt as defined in Section 114. The mens rea requires either direct intention to cause hurt or subjective knowledge of likelihood of causing hurt. If a person throws a stone into a group intending to frighten them, but knowing that striking someone is likely and a stone hits a person causing pain, the offence under s. 115 is complete. In BNS 2023, the maximum fine was substantially modernized and enhanced from ₹1,000 to ₹10,000, while retaining the one-year imprisonment ceiling.
examples: Teaching example (Punch during argument): An accused gets into a dispute with a shopkeeper, loses his temper, and punches the shopkeeper in the face, causing a bloody nose and facial pain. The accused is guilty of voluntarily causing hurt under s. 115(2).

Teaching example (Knowledge without intent): An accused angrily hurls a heavy ceramic mug across a crowded dining hall; it strikes a diner's shoulder, causing acute pain. Even without specific intent to hit that diner, subjective knowledge satisfies s. 115(1).
distinctions: Section 115 vs Section 117 (Grievous Hurt): Section 115 applies to simple hurt (punishing up to 1 year); Section 117 applies to grievous hurt under Section 116 (punishing up to 7 years to life).
Section 115 vs Section 118 (Dangerous weapons): Section 115 applies to simple hurt by ordinary means; Section 118 applies when hurt is caused using dangerous weapons or means.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who slapped a neighbor during a parking altercation, causing ringing in the ears and facial swelling, is punishable under s. 115.
Rule: Voluntarily causing bodily pain by an intentional physical strike satisfies BNS s. 115.
Application: The physical slap was intentional and caused acute pain and swelling.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under BNS s. 115(2).
